author: Rivzz
body:
Application
Age: 16
Timezone: EDT – Eastern Daylight Time / Eastern Daylight Savings
Do you have access to TeamSpeak? Yes/No: Yes
Do you have access to Skype? Yes/No: Yes
Do you have access to a recording software? Yes/No: Yes

CRITERIA 1: SELF REFLECTION/EVALUATION

Do you have any experience as a staff member on any servers?

    My experience as a staff member goes back to early days of 1.4.5 (November 20, 2012). In the early days of my Minecraft career, like most of us I had no idea what I was doing in regards to actually playing the game. Eventually, I figured out how to join a server, and believe me... it was the best feeling in the world! The server I joined was in many cases very classic. There were no staff members online, and if you had a question you'd most likely get told, "Go home kid" by senior members of the community. Unimpressed, I looked into the server some more, and realized that staffing a server correctly is essential to the evolution of the community. After about a month of dealing with the most repulsive people of my career, I decided that I'd create my own server, in my own image.

    I began talking to my father about the idea of creating a Minecraft server. He has a technology career, so he was very excited for me to take things into my own hands. A few days later, my father got an old Dell computer from his office, and brought it home. He had me set up the computer, and learn its basic mechanics. Later on, we installed a Minecraft Vanilla server on the computer and I threw a little party! The next day, I woke up at the crack of dawn, woke my father up (which he protested) and convinced him to take the computer to my grandmothers house. A few hours later, I was sitting down with the old Dell computer in my grandmothers basement wanting
to create a Bukkit server. After several failed attempts, and several tantrums later I got a Bukkit 1.4.5 server to run on the Dell computer. I told my father in excitement, "I can create my own server Dad!". He came into the basement and port forwarded the server for me, and then proceeded to set up Team Viewer so I could access the machine from my laptop at home.

    About a week later, I found a plugin called 'BukkitGames' (Basically a spin off of Hunger Games) and installed it, and all its dependencies onto the machine at my grandmother's house. I ran this server for about a month, and built a small, but heart warming community. About 3 months later, I decided that I actually needed to set up permissions and make a donation system. I recreated the server to match the simple SMP server I had first joined, but this time in my image. I was able to figure out permissions, and setup a Buycraft page. This was the first time in my life that I had ever owned a server, or had to manage one. I learned quickly, but of course with some very obvious mistakes. I put my trust in the wrong people, and after a good 8 months my server was completely destroyed. Out of hope, and out of the will to continue, I decided to return to the everyday player of Minecraft.

    After going through the rest of the school year, I decided to try yet again to make a server in my own image. This time, I created my best server to date, reaching a maximum of 350 players and a community that was exciting and as helpful as could be! I ran, and started the server off of what I'd like to call a "sketchy" hosting company. Nethertheless, I was able to form the best community I've ever seen in a Minecraft server in a little under 7 months. I learned how to not just own a server, but excel at running and operating a server with a large community. Eventually, I yet again grew tired of the server I'd made... with falling numbers and the community going
to a place I'd rather not talk about, I decided to sell my beloved server to an administrator. The server 'mc.tinysmp.net' is still available to play on, however I have not looked at in ages due to my confronting my past mistakes.

What is your biggest weakness and how do you believe it will affect your moderating? What is your biggest strength and how would this affect your moderating?

    I have gone through ups and downs, failure and greatness, and happiness and dispeare in my experiences owning and operating multiple servers in my lifetime. However, if I could take on thing away from all that I've learned is that before you act, you think talk it out, or determine the best course of action. My biggest mistake in all of my staff career, is the fact that I'd react before correctly assessing the situation. I have a kind, but deadly heart when it comes to Moderating a server. I will be the nicest, most caring person on the server... however when someone breaks the rules I will be swift in an action. As I've matured and grown from my original mistakes, I now realize that an action without proper inquiry is an action that will be regretted in the future. Instead of sitting here typing about how much I'd like to erase the mistakes that I've made in the past, I'd like to dicuss the things that I've more importantly learned. Strengths and weaknesses are all opinions, and without these opinions we could not properly assess a situation. I would say that my greatest strength is my ability to talk, and immerse myself into the community. I am able to listen to people's opinions... even if I don't agree with what they're saying. I will take someones opinion, or statement with open arms and give a non-bias and friendly response. The one thing I've never done is hurt or reject someone in a time of need, and I will always keep it this way. I come here not only to apply for a Moderator position, but I come here in a reflection and realization of my past mistakes and how
I can fix, and make sure that they do not happen again.

How do you believe you can help improve the Staff Team?

    Improving the Avicus staff team is something that I'd like to take with an open mind. I am not aware of the problems which may or may not be apparent within the staff ranks, so I am not going to sit here and talk about what I see wrong, and right with the current staff team. I'd prefer to talk about how I can see myself improving through the knowledge and opinions of the current members of staff. Getting knowledge before you act is one of my greatest personal pieces of advice, and there is no difference here. I'm sure in the future, after months of experience of Moderating that I'll be able to respond to this question with an accurate response, however as of now, without correct knowledge I cannot respond to this question without some sort of bias or ignorance.

What qualities does a leader need to have in your opinion? Do you consider yourself to be a leader? Why?

    Leadership is the essential part of any community, and without it any community will fail. Leaders need to be kind, curtious, and good spirited... on the flip side they must also be able to respond and act to situations with  a swift unquestionable respond that is the best for the whole of the community. There is a delicate balance between wanting to be a leader for the people's opinions, and being a leader for what needs to be done. Dedicating your time to only listening to what the people want, will result in loopholes and people slipping through the laws of a society. However, dedicating your time only to what needs to be done will result in the people of the community revolting against your ideology, and quite possibly leading to an other throwing of power. A leader should possess the not only the ability to meet the needs of their people, and the needs of the community but also be able to do the right thing in times of hardship or stress. I will only consider myself a leader after I have the entire story of a situation. I cannot stress how many times I hear people say, "I could run this server better than the owner... he knows nothing about how to operate a server!". However, the reality is they DON'T know the entire story, and therefore they CAN'T properly grasp what actually needs to be done in each situation. Leadership for myself is the ability to self sacrifice for your people. Do not commend your people to do something that you would not do yourself. Coming into any new experience I will not assume control or leadership of something; I will instead  watch the people in the community, learn how they act and respond to situations, and then take leadership when the time is right. 

What attributes distinguish yourself from other players that qualify you to be a moderator?

* This will be the only section where I praise myself for my previous actions. *

    Distinguishing a decent community member from an excellent community member is an accurate way to judge a person's beliefs and ideas. If they just pop in and out of a community, and take but do not give back then they are the  "average" member of a community. An excellent member of a community is someone who sacrifices their time to help others learn and grow. Without these excellent members a community would fail. Judging a person based off of their appearance in a community is only accurate if they are active enough to get their opinions and beliefs out there. Therefore, it is impossible to judge a new member of the community and accurately determine if they are the type of person that you'd want to be around. Through my past experiences Moderating, owning, and operating servers I have come to the realization that the staff members are the essential part of any community. Without these dedicated members, a community wouldn't have a direction, and in a sense would have no idea which path to take. Staff guidance is what keeps a community in check, and determines its future. Distinguishing myself from other applicants is nearly impossible in a single paragraph, or let alone an hour chat on Teamspeak or Skype. I feel that to accurately judge a member of any community they must have a background in the community, and drive to help others and give their services to the community without personal gain. I believe that I have met all of these requirements over the last 3 years of my active services on the Forums and Ingame for Avicus. I really hate to say it like that... but I believe that in the end, the applicants that have backgrounds giving back to the community will be the first priority pick, and I want to make that clearly evident.

What skills do you believe you should have when interacting with the community? Do you believe you have these skills?

    I have been active, and interacting with the community since my first month or so in joining Avicus. I have given back to the community through artwork, ideas, help, and questions which have helped solve problems for other players. I have had one infraction for 'Team Spleefing' on March 7, 2017 @ 10:55 PM. This is a mistake which I always have regretted, but I decided not to appeal it due to a reminder of a past error on my part, and the will to not let it happen again. I have never had any major infractions on Avicus, and I plan to keep it that way. I'd like to believe that my help in the community has helped shape Avicus into what it is today. From the beginning I have offered my ability to draw to the community, and I drew 5-6 characters for players around Avicus. I have even reported two hackers by providing physical video evidence in the Report forum. My goal in the community is not only to help clean it of those who are unwanted, but also to help the community grow and evolve into a community that a player would want to be apart of.

    My skills have matured through years of experience into a combination of well rounded, and ideas essential to Moderating servers. I believe that I can continue my work in the community by providing information to new players, helping to remove unwanted players, and upholding the beliefs of Avicus in their goal to achieve a well rounded and functional community.

How much time can you commit to being a staff member (Rough Idea)? 

    My schedule is as follows;

- Sunday: I have church from 10:30 AM - 11:30 AM. After this I am usually free the rest of the day.
- Monday: I have school from 7:40 AM - 2:20 PM. After this I am usually free the rest of the day.
- Tuesday: I have school from 7:40 AM - 2:20 PM. I have work from 3:00 PM - 8:00 PM at a small BBQ joint near my house.
- Wednesday: I have school from 7:40 AM - 2:20 PM. After this I am usually free the rest of the day.
- Thursday: I have school from 7:40 AM - 2:20 PM. I have work from 3:00 PM - 8:00 PM at a small BBQ joint near my house.
- Friday: I have school from 7:40 AM - 2:20 PM. After this I am usually free the rest of the day.
- Saturday: I am generally free the entire day Saturday, however Saturday is my day to relax, so I might go out with friends.

CRITERIA 2: GENERAL SITUATIONS

You are currently undergoing your junior moderator trial. A ban evader is online and he is constantly ban evading and hacking. You are the only one online and the only one who is able to be online. What would you do?

    I would first get the entire story of the situation. I would ask trusted players, who have been members of the community for sometime. I will then proceed to Freeze the ban evader. I would then proceed to  question the ban evader (EX. Why are you doing this? | What is your goal?). I would then get the story from their side, maybe resolve a solution. After getting their side of the story, and hearing the community's decision, I will then notify staff members of the issue at hand. If no senior staff members are able to login at the time of the issue, then I will catalog the issue (EX. Date | Time | Reason | Username | Chat Log) and leave the player in the Frozen state. I will then wait as long as I can for a senior staff member to come online, and if possible talk to the senior staff member about the issue personally before action is taken.

    If the Frozen user proceeds to login with multiple accounts, I will take the same course of action each time without fail. I will also keep a detailed log of who is Frozen for my own safety as well as records to view if an issue every arises.


Another staff member is constantly joining and harassing other people on Teamspeak in their team channel. The staff member is also referee and has physical permissions to be in that channel. However the leaders do not want this staff member in there and they have asked him to leave multiple times. What would you do?

    My first action would be to log the issue (EX. Date | Time | Reason | Username | Chat Log) in order to refrence evidence for later. If I am familiar with the player who is harassing team members I will ask them to chat, to get their side of the story for my evidence. I would not however reveal that I am doing the log, in order to prevent the player from freaking out, or escalating the situation. Once I have enough evidence, I will either try to diffuse the situation myself, or wait until a senior staff members can deal with the situation. I will also provide my detailed evidence to the senior staff members when they arrive.

A player appeals a punishment you gave them. You realize that the evidence file is corrupted and therefore there is no physical evidence. You know however this person did indeed break the rules, what would you do?

    This is exactly why I keep my own personal log of everything I do. If the online evidence file is corrupt, I will have a personal evidence file to provide for the player's appeal. I would calmly notify senior staff members of the issue at hand, and explain that I have my own personal log of information about the player. I would then present the senior staff members with my own personal evidence.

You are in an Avicus team. One of your teammates is also an Avicus Staff member. One day in your team discord the team member/staff member posts a screenshot of a thread that only staff members can see. The content in the screenshot isn’t very important/confident but only staff members could see it on the forums. If anything, what would you do?

    I would first voice my opinion on the issue to the other staff member about their poor decision in a calm and professional manner. If the staff members does not remove the image, or explain why they posted the image, then I will notify senior staff members about the issue at hand, and provide a chat log and evidence of the situation. If the evidence shown provides passwords or confidential information I will make sure that I notify the player who's information was shown that they NEED to change their password, or information immediately to prevent fraud.

One day the Senior Staff team makes a decision you do not agree with. You do not know all the details of the decision or the circumstances in which they were made and you were simply told by another staff member. However you do not like the decision based from what you know. What would you do?

    I will never make a statement or decision based on half of the story. I will ask around and make sure that I have the entire story before making any statement, or voice my opinion on a decision. I will also take everything that another staff member says with authority and respect. However, if I sense that something is off or wrong with the situation, I will do my own research into the issue. I will then provide my research and evidence to senior staff members with an accurate opinion about the decision.

CRITERIA 3: OTHER
NOTE: This is a new criteria and these questions are less to do with right/wrong answer and more to do with us getting to know you. Please answer these honestly. There is no right or wrong answer.


What would getting moderator on Avicus mean to you?

    Obtaining Moderator status on Avicus would mean the world to me. I have provided feedback, and a sense of community for over 3 years to the Avicus community. One of my secret goals was to obtain a position where I could change and improve the face of Avicus overall. I would not take my position for granted however... I would be overjoyed to hear that I have obtained the status of Trial Moderator!


How passionate are you about Avicus? What does Avicus mean to you?

    My passion from Avicus comes from a long line of Destroy the Monument styled servers. I have always loved the idea of massive Team vs Team games with a common objective. For almost 3.5 years I have come on here to enjoy PvP and teamwork with my friends and family. Avicus is not just another server, its the server that I have always enjoyed and held dear to my heart. I have many great memories of playing Avicus throughout the years, and from my initial login to even today I have never been so passionate about a server, and so excited to play each day.

Do you speak any other languages than English?

I do speak any other languages fluently besides English.

Do you have anything else to add to your application?

    Look... I understand that there are multiple people all going for this position, and I want to respect their goal to achieve Moderator as well. I will not be turned off, or disappointed to play Avicus based on your decision! I want this to be as easy as possible for you the reader... so if you have any questions or concerns feel free to PM me, or email me @ mtjanney2@hotmail.com. Thanks, and have a FANTASTIC Wednesday :)!

imryaan was also a huge help in directing me where to get to get the application format, so kudos to him :D!

A player appeals a punishment you gave them. You realize that the evidence file is corrupted and therefore there is no physical evidence. You know however this person did indeed break the rules, what would you do?

    This is exactly why I keep my own personal log of everything I do. If the online evidence file is corrupt, I will have a personal evidence file to provide for the player's appeal. I would calmly notify senior staff members of the issue at hand, and explain that I have my own personal log of information about the player. I would then present the senior staff members with my own personal evidence.

You are in an Avicus team. One of your teammates is also an Avicus Staff member. One day in your team discord the team member/staff member posts a screenshot of a thread that only staff members can see. The content in the screenshot isn’t very important/confident but only staff members could see it on the forums. If anything, what would you do?

    I would first voice my opinion on the issue to the other staff member about their poor decision in a calm and professional manner. If the staff members does not remove the image, or explain why they posted the image, then I will notify senior staff members about the issue at hand, and provide a chat log and evidence of the situation. If the evidence shown provides passwords or confidential information I will make sure that I notify the player who's information was shown that they NEED to change their password, or information immediately to prevent fraud.

One day the Senior Staff team makes a decision you do not agree with. You do not know all the details of the decision or the circumstances in which they were made and you were simply told by another staff member. However you do not like the decision based from what you know. What would you do?

    I will never make a statement or decision based on half of the story. I will ask around and make sure that I have the entire story before making any statement, or voice my opinion on a decision. I will also take everything that another staff member says with authority and respect. However, if I sense that something is off or wrong with the situation, I will do my own research into the issue. I will then provide my research and evidence to senior staff members with an accurate opinion about the decision.

CRITERIA 3: OTHER
NOTE: This is a new criteria and these questions are less to do with right/wrong answer and more to do with us getting to know you. Please answer these honestly. There is no right or wrong answer.


What would getting moderator on Avicus mean to you?

    Obtaining Moderator status on Avicus would mean the world to me. I have provided feedback, and a sense of community for over 3 years to the Avicus community. One of my secret goals was to obtain a position where I could change and improve the face of Avicus overall. I would not take my position for granted however... I would be overjoyed to hear that I have obtained the status of Trial Moderator!


How passionate are you about Avicus? What does Avicus mean to you?

    My passion from Avicus comes from a long line of Destroy the Monument styled servers. I have always loved the idea of massive Team vs Team games with a common objective. For almost 3.5 years I have come on here to enjoy PvP and teamwork with my friends and family. Avicus is not just another server, its the server that I have always enjoyed and held dear to my heart. I have many great memories of playing Avicus throughout the years, and from my initial login to even today I have never been so passionate about a server, and so excited to play each day.

Do you speak any other languages than English?

I do speak any other languages fluently besides English.

Do you have anything else to add to your application?

    Look... I understand that there are multiple people all going for this position, and I want to respect their goal to achieve Moderator as well. I will not be turned off, or disappointed to play Avicus based on your decision! I want this to be as easy as possible for you the reader... so if you have any questions or concerns feel free to PM me, or email me @ mtjanney2@hotmail.com. Thanks, and have a FANTASTIC Wednesday :)!

imryaan was also a huge help in directing me where to get to get the application format, so kudos to him :D!
